description: Peoria, AZ real estate with Teigh Wade, REALTOR®: Vistancia, Trilogy, Lake Pleasant, Old Town, Loop 101 and Loop 303, school districts and HOA tips.
summary: Peoria is an incorporated city that runs from Old Town near Grand Avenue north past Loop 303 to Lake Pleasant, mostly in Maricopa County with a northern piece in Yavapai County. Housing ranges from older in-town homes to master-planned Vistancia, where Trilogy is 55+. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, helps buyers and sellers across Peoria.

sections.h2: Why Peoria covers so much ground
sections.html:
Peoria is long and narrow. Its southern end, near Grand Avenue and 83rd Avenue, is the original town, settled starting in 1886 by newcomers from Peoria, Illinois, who named their new home after the old one. The city incorporated in 1954 and has since grown north across the desert, annexing Lake Pleasant in 1996. A northern portion even crosses into Yavapai County.

That shape means the Peoria experience changes a lot depending on latitude. South Peoria has older neighborhoods, shopping along the main arterials and the Old Town district. The middle of the city, around Loop 101 and the Peoria Sports Complex, is the busiest commercial area. North Peoria, along Lake Pleasant Parkway and Loop 303, has the newest master-planned communities and desert hills such as Sunrise Mountain, Calderwood Butte and Twin Buttes.

• Peoria Sports Complex opened in 1994 as the first spring training site in the county shared by two teams. The San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners still train there, and the P83 entertainment district surrounds it along 83rd Avenue.
  • Lake Pleasant Regional Park, on the Agua Fria River in north Peoria, offers marinas, fishing, kayaking, camping and scuba diving.
  • Old Town Peoria has the Peoria Center for the Performing Arts and historic buildings such as the 1918 Edwards Hotel, the 1920 flatiron-style John L. Meyer building and the 1920 Paramount Theatre.
  • Paloma Community Park opened in 2020, one of the newer additions to the city's park system.

Vistancia

Vistancia is a large master-planned community in north Peoria near the Loop 303 corridor, with views of the surrounding buttes and mountains. Amenities include golf, recreation centers, an aquatic park, tennis courts, parks and a paved trail network. It has several distinct parts, and buyers should know which one a home is in.

Trilogy at Vistancia

Trilogy at Vistancia is a 55+ age-restricted community inside Vistancia, built from 2004 on with Shea Homes as the original designer. It has the Kiva Club and the newer Mita Club, a spa, pools, and the Trilogy Golf Club, a par-72 course designed by Gary Panks.

Blackstone at Vistancia

Blackstone is a distinct neighborhood within Vistancia, and David Weekley Homes bought its final parcels for recent phases. Ask about any separate association or club fees that apply there.

Terramar and the northeast

Terramar and other neighborhoods in Peoria's northeast corner are served by Deer Valley Unified School District rather than Peoria Unified, a detail buyers often miss.

Peoria was still a small town in 1970. Growth tied to Luke Air Force Base, air conditioning and the postwar building wave turned it into a large suburb, so most of its housing was built from the 1970s onward. As a general pattern, the oldest homes are near Old Town and Grand Avenue, where some neighborhoods have no HOA, and construction gets newer as you travel north. Vistancia and the other north Peoria communities are mostly from the 2000s to today, with builder phases still opening.

Expect stucco exteriors, tile roofs, two-car and three-car garages and planned subdivisions with community associations in most of the city.

Detached homes are the majority, with some townhomes and condos mixed in. Pools, desert landscaping and rooftop solar are common sights.

1. Read the HOA package. Vistancia and other master plans can have a master association, a sub-association and separate club or gate fees. Ask what each covers and what is charged at closing.
  2. Confirm the age rules. Trilogy at Vistancia is 55+. Make sure the home and the buyer meet the community's requirements before the contract.
  3. Check the utility provider. APS serves most of Peoria, with some areas on SRP. The city relies heavily on Central Arizona Project water.
  4. Ask about solar. Owned, financed and leased systems each transfer differently.
  5. Inspect the pool. Have a pool specialist look at the equipment, surface and barrier.
  6. Look at lot position. In the hills of north Peoria, slope, drainage and view lots affect both price and maintenance.

For the full process, see how Teigh helps buyers find and close on a home.

Loop 101 runs through the middle of the city and connects to I-10 to the south and I-17 to the east. Loop 303 crosses north Peoria near Vistancia and Lake Pleasant Parkway. US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the south end through Old Town. Lake Pleasant Parkway is the main north-south route in the north, and Northern Parkway is being built out across south Peoria.

Peoria Unified School District serves most of the city. Deer Valley Unified School District serves parts of the northeast, including Terramar. Nadaburg Unified serves parts of the northwest, and Wickenburg Unified serves the Yavapai County portion. Confirm the assigned schools for any address with the district before you decide.

Peoria buyers usually ask three things right away: what the HOA dues and club fees are, whether solar is owned or leased, and how old the roof and AC units are. In north Peoria they also ask about views, lot premiums and gated access. In older south Peoria neighborhoods they want to know about updates to plumbing, electrical and windows.

faqs.q: Is Peoria, AZ in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: Mostly. Peoria is an incorporated city that lies mainly in Maricopa County, with a northern portion in Yavapai County. It incorporated in 1954 and annexed the Lake Pleasant area in 1996. Check the county on the parcel record, since it affects property taxes and some services.

Vistancia as a whole is not age-restricted. It is a master-planned community with several parts, and one of them, Trilogy at Vistancia, is a 55+ age-restricted community. Other areas, including Blackstone at Vistancia, are not part of Trilogy. Confirm which section a home is in before you make an offer.

faqs.q: Who trains at the Peoria Sports Complex?
faqs.a: The San Diego Padres and Seattle Mariners hold spring training at the Peoria Sports Complex, which opened in 1994. It was the first spring training facility in the county shared by two Major League teams. The P83 entertainment district along 83rd Avenue surrounds the complex.

Yes. Lake Pleasant is a reservoir on the Agua Fria River in north Peoria, annexed by the city in 1996. Lake Pleasant Regional Park offers marinas, boating, kayaking, fishing, camping and scuba diving. Lake Pleasant Parkway connects the lake area to the rest of the city.

Loop 101 runs through the middle of Peoria, and Loop 303 crosses the north end near Vistancia. US-60 (Grand Avenue) runs along the south end through Old Town. Lake Pleasant Parkway is the main north-south road in north Peoria, and Northern Parkway is being extended across the south.

Peoria Unified School District serves most of the city. Deer Valley Unified serves parts of the northeast, including Terramar, Nadaburg Unified serves parts of the northwest, and Wickenburg Unified serves the Yavapai County section. Confirm the schools assigned to a specific address directly with the district.

faqs.q: Does Peoria have APS or SRP?
faqs.a: Arizona Public Service (APS) provides electricity to most of Peoria, and Salt River Project (SRP) serves some customers. Water comes largely from the Central Arizona Project. The provider depends on the address, so confirm it when you compare homes and estimate monthly costs.

Peoria values depend on the community, lot, view, age, condition and upgrades, so a single citywide number would mislead you. Teigh prepares a comparative market analysis using recent sales and active competition near your home. Request one on the home value page or reach Teigh by call or text to talk it over.
